header.running_head: Honouring People Despite Differences in Opinion and Deed

blocks.text: Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that when Ibn Jurmooz (the person who martyred Hadhrat Zubayr (RA)) sought permission to see Hadhrat Ali (RA), the Khalifah was very unwilling to see him. "(Is this how you treat) Those who fought hard (for you)?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "Take sand in your mouth! I have every hope that Talha, Zubayr and I shall be amongst those about whom Allaah says:

blocks.arabic_text: وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِيْ صُدُوْرِهِمْ مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَانًا عَلٰى سُرُرٍ مُّتَقٰبِلِيْنَ
blocks.text: We shall remove any ill-feelings that may be in their breasts. As brothers they will be seated on couches, facing each other."[^1]
Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) Rebukes those who Spoke Ill of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)

Hadhrat Amr bin Ghaalib reports that when Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA)[^2] overheard someone speak ill of Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), he said, "Be quiet! May you remain deprived of good and sworn at! I testify that she shall definitely be the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ in Jannah."[^3] Another narration adds that Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) said to the man, "Get away! May you be deprived of all good! Are you insulting the beloved of Rasulullaah ﷺ?"[^4]

Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) once said, "Our mother Aa'isha (RA) had her own opinion. We know for sure that she is the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ in this world as well as in the Aakhirah, but Allaah used her to test whether it was He (Allaah) Whom we obeyed or her."[^5]

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) sent Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) and Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) to Kufa to rally people to fight, Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) addressed the people saying, "I know well that she (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)) is the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ in this world as well as the next, but Allaah is using her to test if it is He (Allaah) Whom we obey or her."[^6]
Following The Elders Despite Believing Differently
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Instructs that Hadhrat Umar (RA) be Followed
Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab reports, "I once went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood
